correctness.rationale: The union/support map and all-pairs map give equivariant inverse order homotopies; an open common neighbor exists exactly when two labels are unused. The rank-selected complex and crown graph are full subcomplexes on complementary vertex classes of the barycentrically subdivided simplex sphere, so renormalizing the middle-rank barycentric weights gives the asserted equivariant deformation retraction off the graph. Translation acts freely on the centered sphere for prime p and its Fourier weights are 1 through (p−1)/2. The graph quotient has parallel edges, so the natural quotient cell structure need not be interpreted as an abstract simplicial triangulation; the embedded graph is unambiguous. Lifting e_a e_b^{-1} from L_0 ends at L_{a−b}, with the prescribed sign convention. The rank-selected Boolean wedge theorem gives p²−3p+1 spheres in dimension d=p−4, so the free cover is simply connected and the quotient has π₁=C_p. In homological Cartan–Leray the only positive cover row has degree d, so below d the base-row groups give odd-degree Z/p and vanishing positive even-degree groups. Top homology is free and χ=(1−(p²−3p+1))/p=−(p−3) gives rank p−2. In cohomology the base row is also injective at degree d, because the only possible source for an incoming differential there is in negative column; thus the top-degree mod-p class v u^{(d−1)/2} survives. At most one degree-one factor can occur in a nonzero product and all others have degree at least two, which proves the matching cup-length upper bound. Integral powers and products with top classes follow from the low-degree ring identification and the d-dimensional model. For p=7 these arguments give d=3, χ=−4 and top rank 5. The stated field checks support that case but do not establish the prime-uniform result.
residual_risks: The claim is homotopy equivalence, not a homeomorphism of the finite quotient with an open complement. No quotient CW or general claim is inferred from the p=5 diagnostic.

originality.rationale: The exact prior equivariant crown model is stronger overlap than an action on homology alone: it gives both vertex classes in the same sphere and the renormalization construction, in the opposite complement direction. The underlying complement retraction and passage to a free lens quotient are consequently close deductions, not independent new machinery. The supported distinct result is the described ordinary quotient with a computed inclusion of the embedded graph on fundamental groups, together with the exact quotient groups and the top-degree surviving product in the odd-dimensional model. The available same-complex source stops at the covering complex's signed integral module; the earlier cup-length computation concerns a different cover and uses a product below the top-dimensional cutoff. No coverage of the entire stated model and its invariants is established by those comparisons.
residual_risks: The known equivariant model makes the geometric reduction accessible. An earlier explicit prime-cycle specialization with the same voltage and cohomology may exist; not all classical full texts were inspected. No priority finding is made from dates or catalogue silence.

The specified embedded graph, including the winding of its loops and surjectivity onto the ambient cyclic group, gives more information than a count of removed edges or a generic lens-space skeleton.
